Every interview scheduled in Lever on one day, across all active candidates, each with the candidate's name and link, the role, and its start time written for a person. Cancelled interviews and archived candidates are left out. by_interviewer groups them per interviewer with their email and ready-to-send lines, so 'email each interviewer their interviews today' needs no loop over candidates, date filter, posting lookup or grouping step. list_stalled_candidates.description: (beta) List the active candidates who have been in their current pipeline stage for more than a number of days, reading every page of Lever itself. Archived candidates (hired, rejected, withdrawn) are left out. Each candidate comes with their name and email, the stage's name, how many days they have waited, the job they applied to, a link that opens them in Lever, and the name and email of their owner: the Lever user responsible for them, usually the recruiter. The same candidates are also grouped in `by_owner`, one record per owner with that owner's `candidates`, so emailing each recruiter their own list is a loop over `by_owner` that sends `candidates` as a table to `owner_email`. Candidates with no owner are in one group whose `owner_email` is "". Nothing else is needed: no paging, date arithmetic, stage lookup or user lookup.

lever_new_opportunity_trigger.description: Runs for each new opportunity in Lever. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object: the opportunity (one person's candidacy for a job) as Lever returns it. id; name (the candidate's name); headline; emails (a list); location; origin; tags and sources (lists); stage (the id of the pipeline stage it is in, not the name: Get stage gives the name); owner (the id of the Lever user responsible for it, usually the recruiter, not a name or email: Get user gives both); contact (the person's contact id); applications (a list holding the application's id); urls.show (the link that opens the candidate in Lever); createdAt, updatedAt, lastInteractionAt, lastAdvancedAt (when it reached its current stage); archivedAt and archiveReason (null while the candidate is active); stageChanges (each move: toStageId, userId, updatedAt). Every time is in epoch milliseconds (milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC), not a date.
